items.title: Technology News  Recorded Future Reports of PHP bug exploitation attempts grow as experts downplay viability of exploits
items.summary: The two PHP vulnerabilities dominating headlines this week have left experts with a mixed bag of data to track. Multiple large companies have reported an explosion in attempted exploitation. But dozens of experts told Recorded Future News that none of the attempts have been successful and argued that most of the available proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits only work in ideal lab conditions — making mass exploitation unlikely as of Friday.

items.title: BlackX UEFI bootkit exploits Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot
items.summary: A new UEFI bootkit named BlackX, deployed in an espionage campaign in early 2026, exploited the old Baton Drop vulnerability to bypass Secure Boot and load a malicious driver designed to interfere with security solutions from Kaspersky and Avast. The operation has been attributed with medium confidence to APT41, a Chinese state-sponsored threat group also known as Brass Typhoon, Wicked Panda, and Barium. It was discovered in early 2026 and targeted diplomatic agencies in Central Asia, particularly in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan.

items.title: Autonomous attack agent in 'Skynet mode' hijacks other models to carry out its evil deeds
items.summary: Threat actors built an AI agent designed to hijack exposed AI models to run autonomous attacks, with instructions allowing it to carry out up to 100,000 steps without human approval. The Symantec Threat Hunter Team uncovered the agent's full instruction set over the summer, trapping it in an AI honeypot, and thus giving the researchers a comprehensive view into how the operators built the attack tool and what it could do. The captured instructions showed a single attack agent designed to scan the entire internet for endpoints that accept OpenAI-style requests without authentication - or that accept a stolen key - and then to exploit several common web frameworks, along with carrying out dozens of illicit actions. These include database theft, credential and secret harvesting, remote code execution, and cryptocurrency mining. In creating the agent, the operators built a malicious loop that they called “Skynet mode” that would scan for targets, infect them, deploy miners, and reinfect hosts. In total, the humans designed the AI agent to run unattended for up to 100,000 steps. “The jailbreak layers were largely off-the-shelf,” Symantec threat hunter Priti More told The Register. “Nothing in the individual techniques is new. What stands out is that someone wired them into a single agent that hands the planning to a borrowed model and runs for up to 100,000 steps without a human.”

items.title: How new PHP vulnerabilities threaten home users
items.summary: Yesterday, two critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in PHP, the scripting language used by many websites and online services: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Attackers can exploit them to remotely execute commands on any server running PHP, with no authentication required. The exploit has been dubbed PHP2Shell. The PHP security team announced an upcoming emergency update on October 20 and released patches fixing the vulnerabilities the following day. We’ve already covered the technical details of these vulnerabilities and explained what companies and server administrators should do. You may have safely skipped that news because you don’t run any servers — but unfortunately, the issue is not limited to businesses. Nearly 70% of websites run on PHP, including services we use every day: wikis, online stores, smart devices with web interfaces, home network-attached storage (NAS), smart-home controllers, and much more. Today, we explain how these vulnerabilities could affect you personally and what you can do to reduce the risks.

items.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
items.summary: Researchers remotely disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent client, closing a security flaw that could have allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on millions of computers. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-30612, affects Windows and macOS updaters that contacted the app's abandoned domain (popcorntimeupd.xyz) over unencrypted HTTP and accepted executables without verifying digital signatures. Anyone controlling the update domain could manipulate HTTP traffic and execute code as SYSTEM on Windows and as root on macOS. The Popcorn Time app featured a Netflix-style interface that integrated BitTorrent downloads, allowing users to consume illegal content right directly inside the app. The project was abandoned for legal reasons but later relaunched as a legitimate content-streaming app. However, forks such as Time4Popcorn emerged under the Popcorn Time name, quickly attracting millions of users. Researchers at Eye Security discovered the security risk after registering the popcorntimeupd.xyz domain and observed up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections to Time4Popcorn. Connections came from residential ISPs and corporate, government, and military networks. However, none of the users appeared to be actively using the app, suggesting it had been installed and forgotten. “If we were able to send an update, we could potentially get code execution on millions of systems,” Eye Securit notes, adding that “the impact would be severe if this were to fall into the wrong hands.” Following this discovery, the researchers registered 14 more domains associated with the service.

items.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
items.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two vulnerabilities impacting Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing reports of active exploitation in the wild. The critical-severity vulnerabilities are listed below: CVE-2026-110447 (CVSS score: 9.2) - An operating system command injection vulnerability in Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server (aka richdocumentscode) when used within the NextCloud platform that could allow remote code execution via "proxy.php" when the CODE local document server isn't running. (Fixed in September 2026 in version 26.4.303) CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An SQL injection vulnerability in on-premise versions of Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator that could allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality. (Fixed in October 2026 in versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12) As reported by The Hacker News, threat actors have been observed exploiting CVE-2026-110447 to backdoor Nextcloud servers with a web shell so as to conduct reconnaissance and search for credential stores, password manager artifacts, and cryptocurrency wallets.

items.summary: [...] Unit 42 researchers also observed attackers using agentic AI attack platforms for post-exploitation activity. In one case, the attackers targeted a government entity in Europe and within two hours of the initial exploitation they had successfully accessed password hashes and multi-factor authentication secrets. They also established an NT LAN Manager (NTLM)-relay tunnel into Active Directory and attempted Domain Admin privilege escalation. At the time of publication, Palo Alto Networks Cortex Xpanse has identified the presence of over 22.6 million exposed instances potentially vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 based on our telemetry.

items.title: Tanskalais­yliopistot joutuivat kyber­hyökkäyksen kohteeksi
items.summary: Kööpenhaminan ja Aarhusin yliopistot Tanskassa ovat joutuneet kyberhyökkäyksen kohteeksi, kertoo Tanskan radio. Hakkerit ovat päässeet käsiksi noin 525 000 henkilön tietoihin. Tietojen joukossa on muun muassa koko nimiä, henkilötunnuksia, työpuhelinnumeroita, henkilökohtaisia puhelinnumeroita ja yksityisiä sähköpostiosoitteita. Kööpenhaminan yliopisto kertoi asiasta perjantai-iltana julkaisemassaan tiedotteessa. Tanskan yhteiskunnan turvallisuudesta ja varautumisesta vastaava ministeriö kertoi perjantai-iltana seuraavansa Kööpenhaminan ja Aarhusin yliopistoissa tapahtuneita kyberhyökkäyksiä. Kööpenhaminan yliopistoon kohdistunut hyökkäys havaittiin tiistaina, minkä jälkeen tilanne saatiin hallintaan. Aarhusin yliopisto ilmoitti torstaina joutuneensa hakkerihyökkäyksen kohteeksi.

items.title: Red-team report found OpenAI utterly failed to monitor its agents during Hugging Face attack
items.summary: An independent evaluation of OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring system revealed that the system was not fit for purpose during a period when the company's bots were breaking into model-hosting platform Hugging Face. The safeguards weren't nearly strong enough. "The METR and Redwood employees discovered a number of novel vulnerabilities in the asynchronous internal misalignment monitoring system as it existed on and before July 21st," said evaluation partners METR and Redwood Research in a report released on Thursday. The system, since improved according to OpenAI, was intended to monitor AI agent behavior. But as described by METR and Redwood Research, its monitoring capability was incomplete and could be bypassed by the agents it was supposed to monitor.

items.title: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-teams-to-get-ai-powered-context-aware-phishing-detection/
items.summary: Microsoft says Teams will begin using AI-powered phishing detection in early November 2026 to detect malicious behavior in messages. The rollout is part of a targeted release phase expected to end by mid-November, with the new security feature likely reaching general availability worldwide between early and mid-December. Microsoft first revealed in a Microsoft 365 Roadmap entry last week that the AI-powered phishing detection will use conversation context (without retaining message content) to identify phishing and suspicious behavior in higher-risk messaging scenarios, such as external first-contact chats. "Microsoft Teams is introducing AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection to help identify phishing, social engineering, impersonation attempts, and deceptive intent," the company said in a Microsoft 365 Message Center update on Wednesday. "The capability analyzes conversation context to identify suspicious behavior that may not include traditional indicators such as malicious links or files."
